text:
incident-bot: PAGE: Streaming SLO violation detected for model: rwdx-13b/v2 in us-west-2. p95 increased from ~1.1s to 2.0s, p99 spiked to 6.4s over the last 10m. Streaming stall count up 4x. Alert links: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/streams?orgId=1

alex (oncall): ACK. I'm taking the page. starting tracers and collecting top stacks. pinging infra.

priya (sre): i'm up for triage — leaving a breadcrumb: kqos and cgroup configs were touched in the last deploy window? checking.

alex (oncall): running quick health checks:
```
# fetch fleet metrics
curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/v1/query?query=streaming_latency_p99{region=\"us-west-2\"}" | jq .data.result
```

alex (oncall): p99 query shows ~6.1s for rwdx-13b/v2 shards: shard-3 and shard-7 are worst. p95 ~1.9s.

marco (infra): looking at host-level telemetry, I see elevated block IO wait and several gpu memcpy spikes on hosts hosting shard-3/7. grabbing `nvidia-smi dmon` snapshots.

jen (support): any customer-facing impact? have support tickets?

ops-bot: 2 open support threads flagged: #TCK-452 (acme-inc) and #TCK-459 (finlytics). Both report degraded streaming quality and increased tokenization latency.

priya (sre): correlating traces -> many streaming requests hit blocking in the write path while waiting on device DMA (nvme -> GPU memcpy). p99 tails show many requests stuck at kernel blkcg throttling.

alex (oncall): that sounds like IO/cgroup throttling from noisy tenant behavior. can we identify which tenant is generating heavy IO on those hosts?

marco (infra): pulling `iotop -boP` and container process lists. there is a single container (tenant: openplay) doing sustained 600MB/s disk read + large pinned GPU transfers concurrent with the p99 window.

alex (oncall): openplay again. last month we saw some elevated KV cache warmups from them. could be a warmup/eviction storm pushing writeback.

priya (sre): checking cgroup settings: blkio.throttle not configured per-tenant by default in shared pool. However the host kernel shows writeback spikes and blkio.weight for that container is at default. This host also shows high memory-pressure leading to KV cache eviction events. Logs:
```
[2026-03-15T02:03:11Z] kv-cache: eviction: pool=shared-gpu shard=3 evicted=421 pages
[2026-03-15T02:03:12Z] blkcg: leaf 12345 (openplay) wroteback 1.2G in 3s
```

alex (oncall): impact summary to customers: affected streams see occasional full-frame stalls and p99 token lag spikes up to 6s. Affects streaming clients in us-west-2 using rwdx-13b/v2. Likely impacting throughput on long-stream sessions.

jen (support): notified acme-inc and finlytics with temporary mitigation note. advising retry/backoff.

marco (infra): suggested live mitigations:
- apply temporary blkio throttle to openplay container: limit read to 200MB/s
- isolate shard-7 onto a reserved host (migrate) for hot path
- enable per-tenant cgroup cpuset/blkio QoS clamp for shared pool
- if migration not immediate, steer new streaming sessions to dedicated pool with routing override

alex (oncall): let's do rapid mitigations in this order: 1) throttle openplay, 2) steer new sessions away from affected shards, 3) start migration for hottest shard. I'll run the commands and keep notes.

alex (oncall): applying blkio throttle now:
```
echo "8:0 209715200" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/<container-id>/blkio.throttle.read_bps_device
```

marco (infra): confirmed throttle applied. observed host read bandwidth drop from 620MB/s -> ~180MB/s. GPU memcpy spikes reduced in the next minute.

priya (sre): after throttle, streaming stall rate decreased ~70% in dashboard. p99 dropping from 6.4s -> 2.4s within 3m. p95 returning to ~1.2s.

jen (support): relaying update to customers: "we applied a temporary IO throttle to a noisy tenant and are seeing improvement; we are monitoring and will follow up with timeline for permanent fix." :thumbsup:

alex (oncall): routing override to dedicated pool for new sessions applied for model rwdx-13b/v2 in us-west-2. Command: `rbctl route set --model rwdx-13b/v2 --region us-west-2 --pool dedicated-temp-1`

marco (infra): starting live migration of shard-7 to reserved host (host-evac-11). kicking off eviction + container migrate. ETA ~2m.

ops-bot: Automated check: shard-7 now running on host-evac-11, health checks passing.

alex (oncall): monitoring traces. p99 back down to 1.8s and trending. still watching for tail recurrences.

priya (sre): root causes (working hypothesis): openplay triggered heavy sequential reads and aggressive GPU memcpy patterns (warmup or batch ingestion), causing host-level writeback and blkio contention which in turn forced kernel-level stalls for streaming IO on co-located model shards. Secondary factor: default blkio config allowed bursty IO.

marco (infra): immediate actions logged:
- applied temporary blkio throttle to tenant container (openplay)
- migrated shard-7 to reserved host
- set routing override for new sessions to dedicated pool
- flagged host for offline soak and kernel tuning (revisit writeback and blkio throttle defaults)

alex (oncall): customer impact: acme-inc intermittently saw frames >5s, finlytics short interruptions. openplay likely degraded but at reduced throughput now. severity: Sev2 -> working mitigation achieved.

jen (support): will keep customers updated with follow-up postmortem timeline and next steps.

priya (sre): follow-ups for postmortem:
- add per-tenant blkio controls to shared pool runbook
- add KV cache warmup detection to alerting (detect eviction storms)
- consider auto-evac thresholds: if host io > X for Y seconds, auto-evict largest tenant or migrate shards
- test kernel writeback knobs in staging

marco (infra): I'll own infra work: adjust default blkio weights, add auto-throttle capability, and propose a small QoS shim for streaming-critical shards.

alex (oncall): handing off to priya for long window. priya you're oncall for next rotation?

priya (sre): taking handoff. notes saved to runbook: https://runbooks.internal/streaming-tail-latency. I'll keep monitoring for 2h and will coordinate postmortem owner.

alex (oncall): thanks team. leaving logs and commands in incident folder: /var/log/incidents/1765239999/

priya (sre): postmortem owner: marco (infra) to produce root cause and remediation plan; timeline target EOD. I'll validate and add action items.

jen (support): closing immediate customer comms loop. will reopen if any regressions.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, p99 improved to 1.6s. status: monitoring. severity downgraded to low.

priya (sre): final note: keep an eye on other tenants with large KV warmup jobs; recommend a notice to platform customers about best-practices for cache warmups (staggering, rate-limits).

alex (oncall): Acknowledged. handing back to normal ops. nil further action unless recurrence reported.
